summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded software experience in bare-metal C on STM32 microcontrollers, C++ on Arduino, and Python on Raspberry Pi and Jetson. Built interrupt-driven peripheral drivers (ADC, I2C, UART), a Bluetooth wearable, and a networked multi-device system over WebSocket. Troubleshot and resolved 11 integration failures during the capstone, using logic analyzers and oscilloscopes for hardware debugging.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.
Architected a Mixed Reality headset concept using AI-based real-time chroma keying without a green screen; produced full design documentation (claims and BOM).

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place system: Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller linked over a unified WebSocket fabric.

Troubleshot and resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection from dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux.
Deployed the Jetson arm bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart, non-root isolation) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device WebSocket registration.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
